transcript.text: dehumidifer in the garage hasnt collected any water for weeks, fan is runnin. is it broke? its a meaco

Not necessarily. In a garage, the most common reason is that it’s too cold or the air is already fairly dry.

Most Meaco compressor dehumidifiers collect very little water below about 10–15°C, and can stop extracting almost entirely near 5°C even though the fan still runs. They may also spend time in defrost mode.

Things to check:

• Humidity setting/mode: Set it to Laundry / Continuous, or the lowest RH setting (e.g. 35–40%), and leave it for a few hours.
• Tank/drain: Make sure the tank is properly seated, the float is not stuck, and any continuous-drain hose isn’t taking the water away or kinked.
• Air filter and grille: Clean a dusty filter and ensure it has clearance around it.
• Temperature: If the garage is cold, try it indoors in a warmer room for 2–4 hours, ideally where humidity is above 55–60%.
• Listen after 5–10 minutes: A compressor model should usually make a deeper hum/vibration and the air coming out may feel slightly warmer. Fan-only operation can indicate it is not calling for dehumidification, is defrosting, or has a fault.

A useful test: put it in a warm room, set to Laundry/Continuous, close the door, and run it for a few hours. If it still collects nothing and you only ever get fan airflow, it may have a compressor, humidity-sensor, or refrigerant-system fault.

If you tell me the exact Meaco model and roughly how cold the garage is, I can say what behaviour is expected for it.

its the Meaco 20L low energy, garage is cold, about 6 degrees. display says humidity 55% and target is set to 60%, no error codes. I cleaned the filter too, it was a bit dusty. compressor hardly makes any noise, just the fan

At 55% RH with a target of 60%, it is behaving as intended: it thinks the garage is already drier than the setting, so it will usually run the fan only and not start the compressor.

Also, 6°C is very cold for a compressor dehumidifier. The Meaco 20L Low Energy can operate at low temperatures, but water extraction will be much lower and it may spend time defrosting. At that temperature, 55% RH is not especially damp in absolute moisture terms, so there may simply be very little water available to collect.

Try this:

1. Set the target to 40–45%, or select Laundry/Continuous mode for a test.
2. Let it run for a couple of hours.
3. Check whether, after a few minutes, the compressor starts — you should hear a quieter deeper hum/vibration in addition to the fan, and the exhaust air may become a little warmer.
4. Keep doors/windows shut as much as possible.

If it runs in Laundry/Continuous mode at 6°C but still only ever runs the fan, test it in a warmer room (around 15–20°C) for a few hours. If it still does not bring on the compressor or collect water there, that points more towards a fault.

But based on your current readings — garage 6°C, RH 55%, target 60% — no water collection and little/no compressor noise is expected.
